- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast by 1–2% for first 5–7 days.
- After a spike, model tends to overshoot and then gradually decay — apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per subsequent day post-spike.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility bias — dampen forecast variance by 20–30% unless event-driven catalysts are present.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day window; if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 0.3–0.7% per day until convergence.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a peak, model often lags — add 1–2 days of lagged correction: forecast = true outcome - 0.5–1.0% per day for lagged days.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overconfidently assumes continuation of prior trend — apply “sentiment-neutral” correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for 3–5 days if sentiment remains flat.
